condition: coxph_fast() returns NA (attribute converged = NA), and coxph() gives a warning, a coefficient that is not finite, or a standard error above 1e3.
reason: The maximum partial likelihood estimate is infinite: the finiteness condition L < O_T < H in the Details of ?coxph_fast fails, for example when all events are in one group. coxph_fast() returns NA by design, whereas coxph() moves the coefficient towards infinity until its convergence criterion or its iteration limit stops it.

condition: Both converge without a warning of coxph(), the log hazard ratios differ by at most 1e-6, and the score test of coxph() at the coxph_fast() estimate (coxph() with init at the estimate and iter.max = 0) is at most 1e-12.
reason: Both iterations stop by the same rule on the relative change in the log partial likelihood, but at different iterates. This happens after a halved step, where coxph_fast() keeps a bracket of the root (Details of ?coxph_fast); the numbers of iterations may or may not differ. The score test shows that the coxph_fast() estimate is a root of the score, so the difference is within the convergence tolerance of coxph().

condition: coxph() warns that it ran out of iterations, coxph_fast() converges, and the score test of coxph() at the coxph_fast() estimate is at most 1e-12.
reason: coxph() did not converge in 20 iterations, so its value is not an estimate; the score test shows that the coxph_fast() estimate is a root of the score.

condition: coxph() warns that the coefficient may be infinite and does not run out of iterations, both converge, the log hazard ratios differ by at most 1e-6, and the score test of coxph() at the coxph_fast() estimate is at most 1e-12.
reason: The estimate is finite (the score has a root at the coxph_fast() estimate), so the warning of coxph() is a false alarm.
